about.title: Carmel Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Carmel is a small place, and a death here is felt along Ocean Avenue, in the shops on San Carlos Street, and in the neighborhoods off Junipero Avenue. When that loss traces back to someone else's carelessness, California gives certain family members the right to bring a civil wrongful death claim. The most recent final crash records for Carmel show seven injury collisions and no traffic deaths in 2025, which is a reminder that these cases are not only about the road. A fatal fall on a property, a medical error, a defective product, or a collision on the southbound stretch of SR-1 can each give rise to a claim. Standing goes first to a spouse or domestic partner and children, then to certain dependents and heirs. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and it shrinks when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Carmel families, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Carmel Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can confirm where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Is Watched
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county, or state agency may be responsible. Getting connected early protects that timeline.

items.title: Separate From Any Criminal Case
items.desc: A wrongful death claim is a civil action that moves independently of any charges the district attorney may or may not bring. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Carmel recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Does a wrongful death claim still apply here?
items.answer: Yes. Wrongful death claims are not limited to crashes; they also cover deaths tied to medical negligence, unsafe premises, defective products, and care facility neglect. Even for collisions, a Carmel resident may have died on a road elsewhere, and the claim can still be pursued by eligible family members. The question is whether someone else's negligence caused the death, not where it happened.

items.question: What losses can a family recover in a California wrongful death case?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Each category is proven separately and depends on the family's circumstances. An attorney can walk you through what documentation helps.

items.question: What if the death involved a government road like SR-1 or a city street?
items.answer: When a public entity may share responsibility, California requires a formal government claim first, and the deadline is far shorter than two years. Missing it can end the case before it starts. This is one reason it helps to connect with an attorney soon after a death on a highway or city-maintained street.
